title: Place cacheLife inside the cached function
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed lib/catalog.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Verify the function is called in a cache directive scope.
Test cold, warm, stale and expired reads with a controllable origin and documented timing tolerances.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: cacheLife belongs inside the function or component whose cache policy it configures, not module initialization.
alternativeApproaches: Inspect the framework’s nested lifetime rules and measure the outer representation’s effective policy. Avoid hiding unrelated cacheLife calls in generic utilities; keep the lifetime visible at each cached boundary.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
